schema_lineage.purpose: AI-focused evaluation layer using identical sub-pillar IDs for cross-schema score comparison

dfir_capability_taxonomy_v5.0_ai.intent: Evaluates vendors exclusively on their use of AI/ML technologies within each DFIR capability. Scores reflect the maturity, specificity, and autonomy of AI integration — not general DFIR capability.

metadata.framework_alignment: NIST CSF 2.0 & SANS Incident Handler's Handbook — AI/ML Focus Overlay

scoring_scale.meaning_of_zero: No publicly verifiable evidence of AI/ML usage in this capability area

scoring_logic.0: No Evidence: No publicly verifiable evidence of AI/ML in this capability.
scoring_logic.1: No AI/ML: Capability is entirely manual/traditional with no mention of AI, machine learning, or automation beyond basic scripting.
scoring_logic.2: Generic AI Claims: Vendor mentions AI/ML in marketing but provides no technical specifics, named models, documented workflows, or measurable outcomes.
scoring_logic.3: AI-Augmented: Documented AI/ML tools used with human oversight. Specific use cases described (e.g., ML-based alert triage, NLP-driven report drafting). Humans remain primary decision-makers.
scoring_logic.4: Advanced AI: Specialized ML models with measurable outcomes (e.g., detection rates, time reduction). Partially automated workflows with human validation gates. Named AI features or platforms.
scoring_logic.5: Fully Agentic: Autonomous AI systems that plan, execute, and document with minimal human intervention. Governance gates documented. Model performance metrics disclosed. Evidence of agentic orchestration.

source_policy.description: Evidence may come from any credible public source, not limited to vendor's own website. All sources must be publicly accessible and verifiable.

examples: Published case studies from media companies

invalid_sources: Vendor sales pitches without technical detail

PLA.name: Planning & Preparation
PLA.focus: AI/ML integration in organizational readiness and pre-incident capability maturity. How does AI improve preparedness automation, gap detection, playbook design, and exercise simulation?
ai_evidence_signals: ML-driven gap detection and coverage optimization
AI-generated or AI-maintained playbooks
AI-powered tabletop exercise simulation and scoring
Automated forensic readiness assessment using trained models

INV.name: Forensic Investigation
INV.focus: AI/ML integration in evidence acquisition and analytic reconstruction. How does AI accelerate triage, timeline correlation, artifact attribution, and malware analysis?
ai_evidence_signals: ML-assisted triage with automated reasoning and confidence scoring
AI-powered cross-system timeline reconstruction
ML-driven artifact clustering and provenance attribution
AI-assisted malware classification, deobfuscation, and IOC extraction

REM.name: Remediation & Recovery
REM.focus: AI/ML integration in containment, eradication, and restoration. How does AI reduce time-to-contain, automate persistence detection, and validate recovery integrity?
ai_evidence_signals: AI-recommended containment actions with automated execution gates
ML-based persistence pattern detection across endpoints
AI-validated restoration integrity checking
ML-powered ransomware actor profiling and outcome forecasting

PMG.name: Post-Incident Management
PMG.focus: AI/ML integration in lifecycle oversight, reporting, and communication. How does AI improve coordination, quality assurance, executive communication, and lessons-learned extraction?
ai_evidence_signals: AI-generated task plans and automated incident status synthesis
ML-driven quality assurance and audit trail validation
AI-drafted executive communications with source citations
Automated root cause extraction and improvement recommendation

LAW.name: Legal & Compliance
LAW.focus: AI/ML integration in legal admissibility and judicial support. How does AI maintain chain-of-custody integrity, support court-ready documentation, and ensure methodology defensibility?
ai_evidence_signals: AI-assisted evidence triage that preserves defensible provenance
ML-powered court-ready report generation with traceability
Comprehensive logging of AI agent actions in chain-of-custody
Documented AI model validation, error rates, and Daubert alignment

PLA-01.name: Visibility Gap Analysis
PLA-01.expanded_definition: Using AI/ML to identify telemetry blind spots across hybrid environments and generate prioritized, explainable remediation recommendations.
ai_evaluation_criteria: ML-driven telemetry gap detection across endpoint, network, identity, and cloud sources — not just rule-based checks
Automated asset discovery and classification using trained ML models (e.g., device fingerprinting, shadow IT detection)
AI-generated coverage recommendations with confidence scores, risk prioritization, and explainability
Continuous drift detection using anomaly models on log and telemetry feeds to flag emerging blind spots
Evidence of specific ML models, algorithms, or AI platforms used (not generic 'AI-powered' claims)

PLA-02.name: Behavioral Playbook Design
PLA-02.expanded_definition: Using AI/ML to generate, maintain, and dynamically adapt response playbooks based on threat intelligence, incident context, and attacker behavior patterns.
ai_evaluation_criteria: AI-generated playbook drafts from threat intelligence feeds, incident patterns, or MITRE ATT&CK mappings
Dynamic playbook branching that adapts in real-time based on ML-assessed incident conditions
NLP-driven analysis of past incident reports to suggest playbook improvements or new playbooks
ML-based playbook effectiveness scoring and optimization recommendations
Integration of AI-generated playbooks with SOAR platforms for automated execution with human approval gates

PLA-03.name: Tabletop Exercise (TTX) Automation
PLA-03.expanded_definition: Using AI/ML to generate realistic breach scenarios, simulate attacker behavior, facilitate exercises, and automatically extract actionable lessons.
ai_evaluation_criteria: AI-driven scenario generation using threat landscape analysis, industry-specific attack patterns, or generative AI
LLM-powered role-play simulation (e.g., AI acting as attacker, regulator, or media) during tabletop exercises
Automated participant performance scoring using ML analysis of decisions, timing, and communication quality
NLP-powered extraction of lessons learned, action items, and gap identification from exercise transcripts
AI-generated post-exercise reports with benchmarking against industry standards or previous exercises

PLA-04.name: Forensic Readiness Maturity Assessment
PLA-04.expanded_definition: Using AI/ML to assess evidence preservation readiness, benchmark against standards, and continuously monitor forensic collection capability.
ai_evaluation_criteria: ML-assisted correlation of policies, configurations, and log settings against forensic readiness frameworks (ISO 27037, NIST)
AI-driven automated evidence-readiness scoring with specific gap identification and remediation priority
Continuous monitoring using ML models to detect forensic readiness degradation (e.g., log rotation changes, agent failures)
NLP analysis of policy documents to assess alignment with forensic collection requirements
AI-generated maturity roadmaps with prioritized improvement recommendations and effort estimation

INV-01.name: Triage and Scoping
INV-01.expanded_definition: Using AI/ML to rapidly assess incident scope, prioritize evidence collection, and generate defensible triage summaries with confidence scoring.
ai_evaluation_criteria: ML-based alert triage that prioritizes incidents by severity, blast radius, and business impact using trained models
AI-generated triage summaries that cite specific artifacts, IOCs, and data sources with confidence scores
Automated scoping suggestions using ML analysis of telemetry patterns, lateral movement indicators, and historical incidents
NLP-driven enrichment from threat intelligence feeds integrated into triage workflow
Agentic triage systems that autonomously collect initial evidence and generate preliminary scoping reports

INV-02.name: Multi-Hop Timeline Reconstruction
INV-02.expanded_definition: Using AI/ML to correlate events across disparate sources and automatically construct multi-hop attack narratives with evidence-linked timelines.
ai_evaluation_criteria: ML-powered cross-source event correlation across endpoints, network, identity, cloud, and application logs
AI-generated attack timelines that automatically link events into causal sequences with confidence scoring
Graph-based ML models (e.g., knowledge graphs, GNNs) for visualizing multi-hop lateral movement paths
Automated detection of temporal anomalies and event gaps using statistical or deep learning models
Agentic timeline builders that autonomously collect, correlate, and present evidence-linked narratives

INV-03.name: Artifact Source Attribution
INV-03.expanded_definition: Using AI/ML to cluster artifacts, determine provenance, and attribute findings to actors or campaigns with traceable evidence chains.
ai_evaluation_criteria: ML-driven artifact clustering that groups related IOCs, files, and behaviors by likely source or campaign
AI-assisted attribution models that link artifacts to known threat actors using TTP fingerprinting
Automated provenance graph generation connecting artifacts to their origin (process tree, file path, user, network flow)
NLP analysis of malware code, ransom notes, and communications for linguistic attribution signals
AI confidence scoring on attribution conclusions with explicit evidence chain documentation

INV-04.name: Malware and Reverse Engineering
INV-04.expanded_definition: Using AI/ML to analyze malicious code, automate deobfuscation, classify malware families, and extract IOCs and TTPs at scale.
ai_evaluation_criteria: ML-based malware classification and family identification using trained models (not just signature matching)
AI-assisted code deobfuscation and unpacking using deep learning or symbolic analysis
LLM-powered code understanding and natural-language explanation of malware behavior
Automated IOC, YARA rule, and TTP extraction using ML pipelines with validation
AI-driven sandbox analysis with behavioral classification and automated report generation

REM-01.name: Containment and Isolation
REM-01.expanded_definition: Using AI/ML to recommend and execute containment actions with speed, precision, and documented rationale while preserving forensic evidence.
ai_evaluation_criteria: AI-recommended containment actions (EDR isolation, account disable, network segmentation) with documented rationale and blast-radius assessment
ML-based risk scoring to prioritize containment targets and predict attacker next-move to preemptively contain
Automated containment execution through AI-SOAR integration with human approval gates and rollback capability
AI-driven evidence preservation checks prior to containment to prevent forensic data loss
Agentic containment systems that autonomously respond to confirmed threats within defined governance boundaries

REM-02.name: Root Cause Eradication
REM-02.expanded_definition: Using AI/ML to detect persistence mechanisms, generate eradication plans, and verify complete removal across the environment.
ai_evaluation_criteria: ML-based persistence detection that identifies non-obvious mechanisms (scheduled tasks, registry, WMI, firmware) beyond signature matching
AI-generated eradication checklists tied to specific findings with artifact citations and validation steps
Automated scanning using trained models to verify complete removal of attacker footholds across all affected systems
NLP-driven analysis of threat intelligence to identify persistence TTPs specific to the observed threat actor
AI-powered root cause analysis that traces the initial compromise vector using causal inference models

REM-03.name: Recovery and Restoration Verification
REM-03.expanded_definition: Using AI/ML to validate recovery integrity, detect post-restoration anomalies, and ensure hardening measures address the identified root cause.
ai_evaluation_criteria: ML-based anomaly detection on restored systems to verify clean-state (behavioral baseline comparison)
AI-validated backup integrity checking using trained models to detect embedded malware or compromised images
Automated post-restoration monitoring using ML models to flag deviations from expected system behavior
AI-generated hardening recommendations specifically tied to the incident root cause with implementation guidance
Predictive models assessing re-compromise risk based on threat actor TTPs and remediation completeness

REM-04.name: Ransomware Negotiation and Outcomes Forecasting
REM-04.expanded_definition: Using AI/ML to support negotiation strategy, forecast outcomes, and profile threat actors using historical data and behavioral analysis.
ai_evaluation_criteria: ML-powered ransom outcome modeling using historical payment data, actor behavior patterns, and case-specific signals
AI-driven threat actor profiling and TTP clustering to predict negotiation behavior and reliability
NLP analysis of ransom communications for sentiment, urgency signals, and linguistic threat actor fingerprinting
AI-generated negotiation strategy recommendations based on case context and historical outcome data
Predictive models for data recovery probability and decryption key reliability based on actor track record

PMG-01.name: Incident Coordination and Escalation
PMG-01.expanded_definition: Using AI/ML to automate task coordination, generate status updates, optimize resource allocation, and manage escalation decisions.
ai_evaluation_criteria: AI-generated task plans and work breakdown structures for incident response with priority and dependency analysis
Automated incident status synthesis using NLP to aggregate updates from multiple analysts into coherent summaries
ML-based escalation recommendations that assess severity progression and suggest stakeholder notifications
AI-powered resource allocation optimization based on analyst availability, expertise matching, and case complexity
Agentic coordination systems that autonomously track progress, identify blockers, and flag overdue tasks

PMG-02.name: Forensic Quality and Compliance Management
PMG-02.expanded_definition: Using AI/ML to automate quality assurance checks, validate audit trail completeness, and ensure SOP adherence throughout the investigation.
ai_evaluation_criteria: AI-driven QA checks that validate evidence handling procedures against SOPs and flag deviations with traceability
ML-based audit trail completeness validation that detects gaps or inconsistencies in evidence chain documentation
Automated compliance checking against accreditation requirements (ISO 17025, ASCLD) using NLP analysis
AI-generated quality scorecards for investigations with specific improvement recommendations
Real-time SOP adherence monitoring using ML models that flag procedural deviations during active investigations

PMG-03.name: Crisis and Board Communication
PMG-03.expanded_definition: Using AI/ML to draft executive-ready communications, translate technical findings into business impact, and maintain evidence-backed narratives.
ai_evaluation_criteria: LLM-powered drafting of executive briefings and board communications with automatic technical-to-business translation
AI-generated incident summaries that cite specific evidence sources and maintain factual traceability
Automated regulatory notification drafting (GDPR, SEC, HIPAA) using NLP templates adapted to incident specifics
ML-based impact assessment that quantifies business exposure, customer impact, and regulatory risk from incident data
AI-assisted media response preparation with fact-checking against investigation findings

PMG-04.name: Post-Incident Learning and Review
PMG-04.expanded_definition: Using AI/ML to extract structured lessons learned, identify systemic patterns across incidents, and generate prioritized improvement recommendations.
ai_evaluation_criteria: NLP-powered extraction of themes, root causes, and action items from post-incident review documents and meeting transcripts
ML-based pattern analysis across multiple incidents to identify systemic weaknesses and recurring failure modes
AI-generated improvement recommendations with prioritization, effort estimation, and expected risk reduction
Automated benchmarking of incident response metrics against industry baselines using ML comparison models
Knowledge graph construction from lessons learned to enable cross-incident learning and trend analysis

LAW-01.name: Evidence Collection and Preservation
LAW-01.expanded_definition: Using AI/ML in evidence collection workflows while maintaining defensible chain of custody, provenance documentation, and tamper-evident preservation.
ai_evaluation_criteria: AI-assisted evidence triage that prioritizes collection while preserving full provenance metadata and chain of custody
Automated documentation of collection procedures using NLP to generate defensible collection reports in real-time
ML-based integrity verification of collected evidence (hash validation, metadata consistency checking at scale)
AI-driven identification of potentially relevant evidence across large data sets using trained classification models
Automated chain-of-custody record generation that includes AI system identifiers, versions, and decision rationale

LAW-02.name: Expert Witness Testimony Support
LAW-02.expanded_definition: Using AI/ML to produce court-ready analysis, automate report generation with traceable evidence linkage, and prepare defensible methodology documentation.
ai_evaluation_criteria: LLM-assisted drafting of expert reports with automatic cross-referencing to source evidence and exhibits
AI-powered evidence timeline visualization generation suitable for court presentation
Automated consistency checking of expert reports against underlying evidence using NLP validation
ML-based identification of relevant precedents and case law for methodology defense
AI-generated methodology documentation that explicitly describes reproducibility, limitations, and error rates

LAW-03.name: Machine-Inclusive Chain of Custody
LAW-03.expanded_definition: Comprehensive logging and governance of AI system interactions with evidence, including model identifiers, prompts, outputs, and decision rationale.
ai_evaluation_criteria: Explicit logging of all AI agent actions, prompts, inputs, and outputs in chain-of-custody records
Model version tracking and documentation of which AI models processed which evidence at what time
Governance controls preventing untracked AI modifications to evidence or analysis products
Automated audit reports showing AI decision trees, confidence scores, and human override points
Documented procedures for challenging or validating AI-generated conclusions in legal proceedings

LAW-04.name: Admissibility Defense (Daubert Standard)
LAW-04.expanded_definition: Documenting AI methodology validity for legal admissibility, including error rates, reproducibility evidence, peer alignment, and model governance.
ai_evaluation_criteria: Documented AI model validation with error rates, false positive/negative rates, and confidence intervals
Reproducibility evidence showing consistent AI outputs across repeated analyses of the same evidence
AI model governance documentation including training data provenance, bias assessment, and version control
Peer-reviewed or standards-aligned AI methodology documentation suitable for Daubert/Frye challenges
Human review and override documentation for all AI-generated conclusions used in legal proceedings
